title: Cited-answer research assistant for transfer pricing law and local requirements
problem: Central transfer pricing teams cover dozens of jurisdictions while rules change constantly, and general chatbots give answers without clear sourcing.
approach: Aibidia with IBFD data announced TP Aurora, returning cited answers from a curated transfer pricing content set, available from 22 May 2025.
The user opens the cited source before relying on an answer.
Vendor claims 90% less research time (vendor-published; baseline and method not given).

title: General AI assistants used by in-house transfer pricing staff
problem: Small transfer pricing teams carry growing complexity with limited headcount, and routine drafting, research and data formatting take time away from analysis.
approach: Staff use Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude for drafting, research, formatting data and stress-testing authority responses; not integrated with company data.
An accountable professional validates every AI output before it becomes part of the record.
93% of surveyed professionals use AI in some form; 37% report regular use in 2026, up from 18% (vendor-published survey).
who: Aibidia survey; Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic tools

title: Self-service transfer pricing answers for non-specialists, escalating to the specialist team
problem: Transfer pricing teams are small and local finance contacts touch the topic rarely, so recurring policy questions pull specialists away from analysis.
approach: Deloitte Poland offers a GenAI chatbot built on the organisation's own policies; it answers simple questions and routes complex ones onward.
Andersen Australia tested a general AI platform on documentation rules: answers were well structured, but the tool cannot own the conclusion.
A specialist handles escalated questions and reviews before any position or document is relied on. No outcome figures published.

title: AI-assisted gathering of intercompany data from several accounting systems
problem: Year-end transfer pricing analysis is a scramble to pull and standardise data from disconnected systems; 79% in Aibidia's 2026 survey spend over 10% of team time on it.
approach: Plante Moran says AI can aggregate information from several accounting and ERP platforms into one consistent format, reducing manual spreadsheet work.
Webinar speakers say fragmented or manual data should be standardised first.
The team reviews how inputs were prepared and reconciles to ledger and consolidated figures. No outcome figures published.

title: AI-drafted functional and industry analysis, including intangible-asset support
problem: Functional, asset and risk analysis, intangibles assessment and industry analysis rely on interviews and many outside sources, and are the parts of a transfer pricing file authorities most often probe.
approach: PwC Singapore has the model gather website information to explain commercial factors behind margin changes, such as pandemic glove-manufacturing margins.
KPMG US says GenAI can automate industry and functional analyses; BDO Canada says AI cannot determine whether arrangements reflect practice.
A practitioner validates the functional profile with business interviews, and a senior practitioner reviews intangibles conclusions.
who: PwC Singapore, KPMG US, BDO Canada

title: AI-assisted search for comparable companies and benchmarking draft
problem: Benchmarking means searching databases or websites one by one, screening, documenting each decision, calculating ranges and writing the report, which takes hours or days.
approach: The model returns a candidate list from the practitioner's screening instructions; the practitioner then runs recognised databases and a documented screen.
A PwC Singapore senior manager said analysis taking up to 100 hours can, under certain conditions, take about 30 minutes (self-reported).
BDO Canada reports AI benchmarking outputs lacking depth or screening rationale; the practitioner approves each rejection and the final range.
who: PwC Singapore, BDO Canada, RoyaltyRange, Exactera

title: First-draft local file and master file narratives with expert review
problem: Local and master files for many entities repeat similar narrative sections and are updated yearly; an Exactera speaker called check-the-box documents lacking substance the most common mistake.
approach: The professional supplies facts, a GenAI tool drafts the narrative, and the expert reviews, edits and approves.
BDO Canada reports recurring gaps in AI-generated outputs, including documentation that looks complete but lacks audit-ready support.
Functional facts are checked against how decisions are actually handled, with sign-off on method selection. No outcome figures published.

title: AI review of transfer pricing files against country rules and for consistency
problem: Local files must meet country-specific rules that change often, and authorities compare figures across files, reports and returns, so mismatches invite scrutiny.
approach: Exactera announced ExactReport, a Word-based app that reviews a draft against country requirements and suggests edits; offered through an early adopter programme.
KPMG South Africa and Nigeria authors advise reconciling data across statements, files and filings to avoid automated flags.
The preparer accepts or rejects each suggested edit, and a person explains reconciliation breaks before filing.
who: Exactera, KPMG South Africa and Nigeria

title: Central transaction data feeding bulk local file and master file production
problem: Trivium Packaging built local files per entity from emailed data and manual formatting, so small teams prioritised high-risk entities and reviewed each document three to four times.
approach: A platform imports transaction data once and generates editable local files for many entities; which steps use AI is not stated.
Trivium reports a simple local file now takes a few hours versus 2-5 working days (vendor-published case study).
Fortum reports a 65% transaction automation rate (vendor-published); local controllers confirm data and external advisors review rather than prepare.

title: First-draft intercompany agreements from the policy, with clause extraction
problem: Intercompany agreements must match the transfer pricing policy and real flows; Plante Moran says drafting often stalls for weeks at growing companies.
approach: AI drafts an agreement from the written policy; an Exactera interviewee says agents can extract pricing and risk clauses for checking.
Plante Moran says drafting moves from weeks to hours (firm statement, not measured).
Qualified transfer pricing and legal professionals review each draft against actual conduct before finalising.

title: Multi-agent review of intercompany deals across transfer pricing, VAT and customs
problem: The same intercompany transaction has legal, transfer pricing, VAT, withholding-tax and customs consequences that separate teams review in sequence, so inconsistencies show up late.
approach: A TPMinds International 2026 example (organisation not named) used multi-agent workflows reviewing legal, transfer pricing, VAT and withholding-tax implications together before drafting.
A sponsored Nexdigm article says multi-agent workflows can flag cross-reporting inconsistencies before audit; professionals decide the resolution.
No outcome figures published; human checkpoints are not stated for the conference example.

title: Automated intercompany price calculation, invoicing and posting
problem: Kemira calculated transfer prices manually across 62 legal entities in 40 countries, which was heavy work for tax, finance and local teams.
approach: A tailored tool automates segmented P&Ls and fee, royalty and resale-minus calculations, with robotics sending invoices and posting entries to SAP monthly.
Kemira reports hundreds of work hours saved (vendor-published).
The tax team uses the tool for monitoring, with a monthly close review of results and unusual movements.

title: In-year monitoring of intercompany margins against policy ranges
problem: Transfer prices are usually tested after year end, so margin drift is found late; in Aibidia's 2026 survey only 7% formally monitor monthly and 60% rely on Excel and email.
approach: Plante Moran describes loading raw data into an AI tool to build dashboards tracking margins against target ranges and flagging deviations.
A TPMinds recap says organisations already monitor outcomes with AI in real time, without naming any.
The transfer pricing team investigates flagged deviations and decides adjustments; finance owns execution. No AI outcome figures published.

title: Connected transfer pricing knowledge model that flags inconsistencies
problem: Policies, agreements, financial results and audit history sit in different systems, so showing why a position is defensible needs extensive manual investigation.
approach: Aibidia announced TP Intelligence, a connected model that flags inconsistencies and traces findings to source evidence; first release planned December 2026.
In a Helsinki demonstration it quantified a EUR 4.8 million potential risk in one entity (vendor-published demo, not a client result).
A controller, reviewer or auditor follows each flag back to its source evidence.

title: Pre-filing audit-risk screening of intercompany positions
problem: Authorities select transfer pricing audits on indicators such as routine entities at a loss, but taxpayers rarely test their own positions against these signals before filing.
approach: Taxpayer-side analytics score intercompany positions against known authority selection patterns and IRS self-assessment suggestions so documentation can be strengthened.
Exactera claims AI can predict audit vulnerability, with no accuracy reported (vendor-published).
The transfer pricing lead decides whether a flagged position needs more documentation, a price change, a defence or an advance pricing agreement.

title: Drafting and stress-testing audit responses from prior documentation
problem: Audit responses need years of prior files read and consistent answers under deadline; half of respondents in a vendor survey spend 50-200 hours on audit response.
approach: KPMG US says GenAI can review historical documents and formulate responses in transfer pricing controversy.
Participants at Aibidia briefings said they use general AI tools to stress-test responses to tax authorities.
The controversy lead reviews every statement of fact and citation, and an accountable professional approves the submission.
who: KPMG US, PwC Singapore, Aibidia participants

title: Idea: AI-assisted economic analysis in transfer pricing litigation, with tool disclosure
problem: Idea, not a deployment: expert economists could use AI for benchmarking and valuation in litigation, which would make the reliability of the output an evidence question.
approach: An IRS LB&I official said experts must explain inputs, assumptions, methods and AI tools, and that the IRS wants to see formulas.
Proposed Federal Rule of Evidence 707 on machine output: the Standing Committee decided on 3-4 June 2026 not to recommend action.
The testifying expert must be able to explain and defend every input, assumption and method.

title: Idea: AI support for advance pricing agreement and dispute resolution cases
problem: Idea, not a deployment: advance pricing agreements and authority-to-authority disputes are lengthy negotiations with uncertain outcomes.
approach: A KPMG commentary (October 2024) suggests AI could improve case management, support negotiation and predict outcomes from past cases.
Aprio says some authorities are developing models to predict outcomes, without naming any.
Negotiation and position-setting remain with practitioners and competent authorities.

title: Transfer pricing policy modelling and planning-opportunity screening
problem: Policy design and planning need analysis of how entity results, tax rates and new business models interact across jurisdictions.
approach: KPMG US says GenAI can scrutinise global tax developments to pinpoint planning prospects, parse financials and update calculations.
Plante Moran says some companies test subsidiary financials against country tax rates with lightweight models, as a jump-start for an adviser conversation.
The adviser and transfer pricing lead review the model's result before any policy or structure change. No outcome figures published.

title: Idea: AI-use and verification log inside transfer pricing workpapers
problem: Idea, not a deployment: if an AI-assisted position is challenged, a team may not be able to show what the AI suggested versus what a person verified.
approach: Record which AI tools, inputs and review steps were used; BDO Canada, the IRS OPR alert and the Werfel register recommend variants.
It is a governance control around AI-assisted work, not an automation.
A reviewer attests to verification of each AI-assisted section.

title: Bringing recurring documentation in-house, with advisors limited to review
problem: Trivium's documentation cost over EUR 10,000-15,000 per entity, forced prioritising high-risk entities, and outside advisors did not know the company fully, according to its transfer pricing manager.
approach: Documentation work moves in-house onto a central data platform, with advisors used for jurisdiction-specific, technical or high-risk matters and for review.
Trivium says the platform gives a predictable cost while scaling coverage; new cost not stated (vendor-published).
Fortum's stated goal is to use external parties only to review local files.

title: Software platform plus experts delivering transfer pricing work at fixed prices
problem: Traditional advisory engagements take months and cost heavily for repeatable work, and in-house teams question paying advisors mainly for validation and risk absorption.
approach: Commenda advertises about four weeks and USD 9,000 versus USD 60K and six months for traditional advisors (vendor claim).
Aibidia and BIP Law & Tax announced an exclusive Italian partnership with a joint task force for continuous transfer pricing management.
Provider experts review deliverables, and the client explains the business and reviews output.
